name: Search Atlas
subcategory: SEO suite, rank tracking and site audits
tagline: An all-in-one SEO platform with keyword research, rank tracking, site audits, backlink data and an AI agent that pushes on-page fixes to your site.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Every visible feature here is a thin UI over data you cannot generate yourself: keyword volumes, SERP positions across locations and devices, and a backlink index built from a continuous web crawl. An agent can absolutely build you a site crawler, a Search Console dashboard, and a tidy issue list in an afternoon, and that covers the technical audit half honestly. What it cannot do is invent search volume numbers or tell you where you rank in Chicago on mobile without paying someone for SERP scrapes. The white label reporting and the agency seat model are also the actual product for a lot of buyers, and those are org problems, not code problems. Build the audit tool, rent the data.
coreLoopDIY: Crawls your own sites for technical SEO problems and merges the findings with your Google Search Console clicks, impressions and average position data into a local dashboard.
requirements: Google Search Console property you own, plus OAuth credentials for the Search Console API
Optional paid SERP API key if you want real rank tracking beyond Search Console averages
whatYouLose: Keyword volume, difficulty and related-keyword data, which comes from licensed clickstream and index sources
True rank tracking by location, device and SERP feature, which means paid scraping at volume
A backlink index: nobody crawls the whole web on a hobby budget
White label client reporting, seats, and the agency workflow around them
The AI agent that writes on-page changes straight into a live site via a script or CMS plugin
moatNotes: The crawl and the keyword database are the product. The dashboard is packaging.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is stitching together a SERP API, a keyword data vendor, a backlink provider and a crawler, then maintaining all four while the vendors change their pricing under you. Agencies pay on top of that for the white label reports, because the deliverable a client sees is half of what they are buying. And most SEO buyers are not engineers: a suite that already has the numbers in one place beats a local script that has three of the numbers and a TODO comment where volume should go.
notes: The crawler and the audit rules are a weekend; the keyword and backlink databases are not. The moat is a continuously refreshed web-scale index plus licensed search volume data, neither of which you can bootstrap.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user SEO audit and Search Console dashboard. No accounts, no hosted service, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Node 20 with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Express for a small local API, and a server-rendered UI using Express plus EJS and plain CSS. No React, no Next, no Tailwind.

Part 1, crawler:
- CLI command: npm run crawl -- https://example.com
- Respect robots.txt, one concurrent request by default, configurable delay, max page cap in .env.
- For each page store: url, status code, redirect chain, title, meta description, h1s, canonical, meta robots, word count, internal and external links, image count and missing alt count, response time, and content hash.
- Store crawls as snapshots in SQLite so two crawls can be diffed.

Part 2, audit rules engine:
- Rules in a single rules.ts file, each a pure function over a stored page row returning severity (error, warning, notice) and a message.
- Ship these rules: missing or duplicate title, title length out of range, missing meta description, multiple or missing h1, 4xx and 5xx pages, redirect chains longer than one hop, non-canonical self-reference, noindex on a linked page, orphan pages, thin content under a word threshold, images missing alt, duplicate content by hash.

Part 3, Google Search Console:
- OAuth via a local redirect on 127.0.0.1, refresh token stored in .env, never committed.
- Pull the last 90 days of query and page rows: clicks, impressions, ctr, average position. Cache into SQLite so the UI works offline.
- Join GSC page rows onto crawled pages by normalized URL.

Part 4, UI at localhost:3000:
- Issues view grouped by severity with counts and affected URLs.
- Pages table, sortable, showing crawl fields alongside clicks, impressions and average position.
- Opportunities view: pages with high impressions and average position between 8 and 25, sorted by impressions, since those are the cheap wins.
- Diff view comparing two crawl snapshots: new issues, resolved issues, changed titles.
- CSV export on every table.

Explicitly out of scope, do not fake these: keyword search volume, keyword difficulty, competitor keyword data, backlink data, and SERP rank scraping. If a field would require a paid third-party data source, leave the column out rather than filling it with an estimate.

Deliver README with setup steps, .env.example listing GSC client id, client secret, refresh token, crawl delay and page cap, and a seed script that crawls a small public site so the UI is not empty on first run.
